clue.text: Bags animals en masse from a broken vessel

parts.note: to bag game is to pot it, so bags means pots
a herd is a large group of animals together

explanation.surface: A collector stuffs a whole menagerie into sacks salvaged from a shattered ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but here it is a pot or jar; the definition describes a fragment that comes from such a smashed container.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a fragment of earthenware, the piece left over when a pot or jar breaks.

clue.text: Alfresco meal of some such as Pooh?

definitions.text: Alfresco meal of some such as Pooh

parts.words: Alfresco meal of some such as Pooh
parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is a teddy bear, and the teddy bears' outing in the woods in the popular song is an outdoor meal

explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to The Teddy Bears' Picnic, a popular children's song; Pooh is A. A. Milne's teddy bear.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor meal eaten in the open air, the kind teddy bears hold in the woods in the song.

clue.text: Figaro. was noted for such work

definitions.text: Figaro. was noted for such work

parts.words: Figaro. was noted for such work
parts.note: Figaro, hero of The Barber of Seville, was a barber, so his work was cutting hair

explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' hints at music, since Figaro is an operatic character, but the work in question is hairdressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything to do with barbers or hair-cutting, Figaro's trade.

clue.text: Not the sole, occupation of a leprechaun

definitions.text: Not the sole, occupation of a leprechaun

parts.words: Not the sole, occupation of a leprechaun
parts.note: in Irish folklore the leprechaun is a shoemaker, and mending the back of a shoe is his work besides soling

explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' reads as 'only', but it is the underside of a shoe: the leprechaun of Irish legend mends shoes, and this is the other job.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting new backs to shoes is a cobbler's task alongside resoling, and leprechauns are cobblers.

clue.text: Estimates speeds

definitions.meaning: to estimate something is to value or assess it
a speed is a pace, as in going at a great pace

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to assess or value, and as a plural noun it means velocities.

clue.text: Compensation for. being absent from filming?

definitions.meaning: something that balances out a loss or cost
an actor not wanted at the studio is away from the set, so off the set

explanation.surface: An actor asks what payment is due for days spent away from the shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful split of the answer into two words, off and set, the set being where a film is shot.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount that counterbalances a loss is called a counterweight or set-off, exactly what compensation does.

clue.text: Bombast from the cloth

explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' usually means the clergy; here it is literally a fabric. Bombast itself was once padding cloth, so the two senses are linked.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a thick twilled fabric and the pompous, padded speech that took its name from it.

clue.text: Prosecuted oriental kid

parts.note: to prosecute is to take legal action, as when one has sued
E for east is the crossword stand-in for oriental

explanation.surface: A young person from the East was taken to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but it is young goat's leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid leather and this soft napped leather are both used for gloves, and it is often made from young goatskin.

clue.text: Upset: on board, subject to trial

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece on top of the next

parts.note: in a down clue, up-set reads the word set going upwards
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Someone thrown off balance aboard ship faces a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like distress, but this is a down clue, so it splits as 'up set': the word set climbing the column. 'on' stacks that above the board word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be tried or examined is open to trial.

clue.text: Stage director

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach, and the person steering its horses directs it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests the theatre, but it is a stagecoach, and its director is the driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The driver of a horse-drawn coach guides the stagecoach along its route.

clue.text: Dispute involving scouts in teens? No

indicators.note: to involve can mean to entangle or twist together, so these words are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Was there a quarrel among the teenage scouts? Apparently not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' looks like plain linking, but it signals that SCOUTS, IN, TEENS and NO are all jumbled together, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency to argue or a state of disagreement, the quality of being a matter of dispute.

clue.text: The little mockings of Hardy's life

definitions.text: The little mockings of Hardy's life

parts.words: The little mockings of Hardy's life
parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist, published a collection of stories called Life's Little ____; the clue paraphrases that title with mockings for its last word

explanation.walkthrough: The clue rearranges the title of Thomas Hardy's story collection, whose stories show fate turning people's plans against them.
explanation.definitionFit: Situations where outcomes mock intentions, the twists of fate Hardy's stories describe, are cases of cruel paradox.

clue.text: Many are returning 'after him. Fancy!

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the word him in the answer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
taken as written

indicators.note: returning means the word are is read backwards, coming back the way it went

explanation.surface: Lots of people are coming back to follow him; imagine that!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an exclamation of surprise but is the noun meaning a whimsical idea; 'returning' turns the word are round and 'after' puts it behind him.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild illusion or idle fantasy, which is what fancy means as a noun.

clue.text: Patriotic militancy of unwilling fighters

parts.note: a Victorian music-hall song ran 'We don't want to fight, but by ____ if we do', so its singers claimed to be reluctant fighters while beating the war drum

explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from that 1878 British music-hall song, sung during a crisis with Russia; the clue's 'unwilling fighters' are its singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressive, flag-waving nationalism that favours war takes its name from that song's refrain.

clue.text: Tax on gold makes him a deceiver?…

indicators.note: on in this down clue puts the tax word above the gold word

parts.note: an impost is a tax or duty
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A levy on gold turns its collector into a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry. 'makes him a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pretends to be another person to cheat others is a fraud or deceiver.

clue.text: Boy, about five, new and strange

indicators.note: about means the boy's name goes around the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: Noel is a boy's name
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A boy of roughly five years old is a newcomer who seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about five' reads as an age, but 'about' puts NOEL around V.
explanation.definitionFit: Something novel is fresh and unfamiliar, never seen before.

clue.text: … but not :a 'big fiddle where he is concerned

definitions.text: but not :a 'big fiddle where he is concerned

parts.words: but not :a 'big fiddle where he is concerned
parts.note: following on from the deceiver of the clue before, fiddle seems to mean a swindle, but the player of the smallest stringed instrument handles a little fiddle, not a cello or bass

explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from 14 Down, so 'fiddle' seems to be a fraud; in fact it is the instrument, and his is the small one.
explanation.definitionFit: The musician plays the violin, the smallest fiddle, not a big one such as the double bass.

clue.text: Term Amos: devised for a monkey

indicators.note: devised means worked out or put together anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Amos came up with a name for a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' signals that TERM AMOS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmoset is a small South American monkey with a long tail.

clue.text: Sailor allowed fresh-water fish

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
to let is to allow, and let is also its past tense

explanation.surface: A seaman is given permission to catch a river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablet, also called the bleak, is a small silvery European river fish.

clue.text: Where one' perhaps eats before 'a dance

definitions.text: Where one' perhaps eats before 'a dance

parts.words: Where one' perhaps eats before 'a dance
parts.note: split as ..., the clue describes having one's tea before going on to a hop, an informal dance

explanation.walkthrough: A hop is an informal dance; read as TEA'S HOP, the answer is a meal followed by a dance, as well as a café.
explanation.definitionFit: A café serving light meals and tea is a place where one might eat before an evening out.

clue.text: Paris's temple also in Rome

parts.note: Paris has a great domed building of this name, and so does Rome, where the ancient temple to all the gods still stands

explanation.walkthrough: Both cities have a famous building with the same name: Rome's is the ancient temple, Paris's the domed church turned mausoleum.
explanation.definitionFit: The name means a temple dedicated to all the gods, applied to the Roman original and its Parisian imitation.

clue.text: Wild-looking writer

definitions.meaning: gaunt and worn, with a wild expression
H. Rider ... wrote King Solomon's Mines and She

explanation.definitionFit: It means looking gaunt and exhausted, and it is the surname of the Victorian adventure novelist Rider Haggard.

clue.text: One who intends to be less generous?

definitions.meaning: someone who means to do something, a person with intentions
comparing two people, the one who is more stingy

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a joke noun made from the verb 'mean', to intend.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a whimsical noun for a person who means something, and the comparative of stingy.

clue.text: Those who interfere, say, with fruit-trees

indicators.note: say tells the solver to go by the spoken form of the word for busybodies, not its spelling

parts.note: meddlers are people who interfere in others' business

explanation.surface: Busybodies, so to speak, tamper with an orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that the word for interferers is heard, not spelt, giving trees whose name sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The medlar is a small tree grown for its brown fruit, eaten when it is half rotten.

clue.text: Dog's misdoing

annotationWithheld.why: Dog's misdoing (5): the only parse splits the single word misdoing into mis (anagram indicator) and doing (fodder), one word doing two jobs, which the check refuses

clue.text: We who with songs your pilgrimage "(Flecker) .

definitions.text: We who with songs your pilgrimage "(Flecker)

parts.words: We who with songs your pilgrimage "(Flecker)
parts.note: a line from James Elroy Flecker's poem The Golden Journey to Samarkand with one verb left out; the solver supplies the missing word

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue had a dash where the missing word goes: the poem's line is about singers who charm away the travellers' weariness with songs.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to charm or while away pleasantly, which is what the poem's singers do to a long journey.

clue.text: Wild plant. One consumed by Remus's brother

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up inside, so the numeral goes into the other word

parts.note: in the Uncle Remus stories the animals are called Brer, meaning brother, as in Brer Rabbit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wild plant is eaten by the twin brother of Remus.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus's brother looks like Romulus, but Uncle Remus is the storyteller of the Brer Rabbit tales, where brother is said Brer.
explanation.definitionFit: The briar or brier is a wild thorny rose or bramble.

clue.text: Watch' procedure 'and, there can be no crisis, Anthony

indicators.note: there can be suggests the letters can be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells Anthony that if everyone follows the set routine, nothing will go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there can be' signals that NO CRISIS and ANTHONY are rearranged; 'Watch' is the timepiece, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting several timepieces to show exactly the same time is the routine of making clocks agree.

clue.text: Village in Perth. or Peebles

indicators.note: in tells the solver the village is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A small place to be found in one of two Scottish towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth and Peebles are Scottish towns; the answer runs across the end of PERTH, the word OR and the start of PEEBLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorpe is an old word for a hamlet, surviving in many English place names.

clue.text: We may be embarrassed owing to him

definitions.text: We may be embarrassed owing to him

parts.words: We may be embarrassed owing to him
parts.note: embarrassed here means short of money, and owing means in debt to someone, so the person we owe makes us hard up

explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassed' reads as shame, but an old sense means financially stretched, and 'owing to him' means in debt to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom money is owed is the one who makes a debtor's position awkward.
